text:
Marta L: Heads-up — product asked for a Redwood Console dashboard to show KV cache + prefix cache effectiveness across runtime and infra inputs. They want hit rate, evictions, and "reuse by workload" so product/SEs can decide cache sizing and routing policy tweaks. Linking internal doc: https://go/redwood/metrics-kv-prefix (rough draft).

Joel P: Do we have a clear list of signals here? hit rate and evictions are obvious, but what should "reuse by workload" look like? Per-model? Per-route?

Samir K: From runtime side we can emit these metrics with reasonable cost: counters for kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total, prefix_cache_hits_total, prefix_cache_evictions_total. Also a label on prefix cache ops like `workload="team/service"` for reuse tracking. For latency: kv_lookup_duration_seconds histogram. Example PromQL for 5m hit rate: 
```
100 * (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])))
```
For evictions: `increase(prefix_cache_evictions_total[1h])` and for reuse by workload: `sum by (workload) (rate(prefix_cache_hits_total{workload!=""}[5m]))` then divide by `sum by (workload) (rate(prefix_cache_hits_total{workload!=""}[5m]) + rate(prefix_cache_misses_total{workload!=""}[5m]))` to get per-workload hit rate.

Marta L: Cardinality worry — workload label could explode if teams include request IDs or user IDs. Samir, can we control cardinality?

Samir K: Yes — don't use freeform IDs. We should emit `workload` as a coarse identifier: `team/service` or `model:route`. Instrumentation PR will enforce max distinct values and map unknowns to `other`. We can also add a hashed label for debugging but not in production metrics.

Anya S: FYI infra constraints: adding more high-cardinality counters affects Prometheus remote write costs and TSDB retention. If runtime emits per-request labels, it will blow up. We need a rollout plan: start with aggregated metrics (no workload label) -> enable per-workload for a canary namespace -> monitor cardinality in the first 24h. Also please add a feature flag gate so we can kill the extra labels quickly.

DevEx - Kevin: For Console UX, product asked for two views: 1) Global summary (overall hit rate, evictions/hr, average lookup latency) and 2) Drilldown by workload/model/route with top-N table + sparklines. Also want SLO overlays and a button to compare before/after a rollout. Can we export the PromQLs?

Joel P: I sketched PromQLs and panel suggestions in the doc. For drilldown we'll need `topk(20, sum by (workload) (rate(prefix_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(prefix_cache_misses_total[5m])))` to find busiest workloads and then join to compute hit rate per workload. We should also provide a normalized reuse metric: `reuse = hits / (hits + cold_loads)` where cold_loads are misses that trigger upstream work.

Samir K: Implementation notes: runtime will add the metrics in runtime v1.42.0. We'll tag the PR with `metrics:kv-prefix`. Will default to emitting only aggregated metrics; per-workload toggled by config flag `metrics.enable_workload_labels`. Also will add an internal sidecar endpoint that maps hashed workload to readable name for the Console (not in TSDB).

ops-bot: deploybot: runtime@canary (v1.42.0-canary.3) rolled out to canary cluster at 2025-09-08T11:23:40Z — metrics endpoint available.

Marta L: Nice. Action items for this thread:
- Samir: open the instrumentation PR and include example PromQL snippets + tests for label cardinality (due EOD tomorrow).
- Anya: prepare a short runbook to revert workload labels and monitor cost (cc infra billing) — add threshold alert if unique label series increase > 10% in 24h.
- Kevin: wire up two Console panels (global + drilldown top-N) using the PromQLs in the doc; add SLO overlay toggle.
- Joel: update the doc with UX copy for the drilldown and per-route granularity.

Will follow up after canary metrics stabilize. :thumbsup:
